subject: Cloud Computing
title: Choosing the Right Storage Tier
description: One-minute skill: Choosing the Right Storage Tier.

hook.text: Storing 1 TB in S3 Standard costs $23/month. In S3 Glacier Deep Archive, it costs $1/month. Same data.

buildup.text: Cloud storage comes in tiers: hot (frequent access), warm (occasional), and cold (rare archival access).

discovery.text: Moving rarely accessed data to cold tiers can cut storage costs by 95% with no change in functionality.

twist.text: Cold storage charges retrieval fees. Access archived data too often and you'll pay more than hot storage.

climax.text: Lifecycle policies automatically move aging data to cheaper tiers. Set it once and savings compound forever.

punchline.text: Hot data pays hot prices. Archive the cold stuff.

quiz.question: What is the risk of moving data to cold storage tiers?
options: Retrieval fees can exceed hot storage costs if data is accessed frequently
Cold storage automatically deletes data after 30 days
Data in cold storage cannot be encrypted

details.summary: Cloud storage tiers trade access speed for cost. Hot storage is fast and expensive, cold is slower and cheaper, archive is cheapest but retrieval takes hours. Matching data to the right tier based on access frequency is one of the simplest ways to cut storage costs.
details.whyItMatters: Most organizations store the majority of their data in hot storage even though 80 percent of it is rarely accessed. Proper tiering can reduce storage costs by 50 to 80 percent.
takeaways: Hot storage suits frequently accessed data
Cold and archive tiers suit rarely accessed compliance or backup data
Intelligent tiering automates placement based on access patterns

faq.question: How does intelligent tiering work?
faq.answer: Services like S3 Intelligent-Tiering monitor access patterns and automatically move objects between tiers. Frequently accessed objects stay in hot storage while untouched objects move to cold. A small monitoring fee per object is charged but savings typically far exceed this cost.

faq.question: What is the cost difference between storage tiers?
faq.answer: As a rough guide, standard S3 costs about $0.023 per GB/month, infrequent access about $0.0125, and Glacier Deep Archive about $0.00099. That makes archive storage roughly 95 percent cheaper than hot storage, with the tradeoff of hours-long retrieval times.
